segments.arabic: [880] وقال محمود حدثنا أبو أسامة قال: حدثنا هشام بن عروة قال: أخبرتني فاطمة بنت المنذر عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر
segments.english: And Mahmud said: Abu Usamah related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us. He said: Fatimah bint al-Mundhir informed me, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr:

segments.arabic: قالت دخلت على عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها والناس يصلون قلت: ما شأن الناس فأشارت برأسها إلى السماء فقلت: آية فأشارت برأسها أي نعم قالت فأطال رسول الله ﷺ جدا حتى تجلاني الغشي وإلى جنبي قربة فيها ماء ففتحتها فجعلت أصب منها على رأسي فانصرف رسول الله ﷺ وقد تجلت الشمس فخطب الناس وحمد الله بما هو أهله، ثم قال: أما بعد وقالت ولغط نسوة من الأنصار فانكفأت إليهن لأسكتهن فقلت لعائشة ما قال: قالت: قال: ما من شيء لم أكن أريته إلا قد رأيته في مقامي هذا حتى الجنة والنار وإنه قد أوحى إلي أنكم تفتنون في القبور مثل أو قريبا من فتنة المسيح الدجال يؤتي أحدكم فيقال له ما علمك بهذا الرجل فأما المؤمن أو قال الموقن شك هشام فيقول هو رسول الله هو محمد ﷺ جاءنا بالبينات والهدى فآمنا وأجبنا واتبعنا وصدقنا فيقال له نم صالحا قد كنا نعلم إن كنت لتؤمن به وأما المنافق أو قال المرتاب شك هشام فيقال له ما علمك بهذا الرجل فيقول لا أدري سمعت الناس يقولون شيئا فقلته
segments.english: She said: I went in to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, while the people were praying. I said, ‘What is happening with the people?’ She pointed her head towards the sky. I said, ‘A sign?’ She nodded her head, meaning yes. She said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prolonged it greatly, until faintness overcame me. Beside me was a waterskin containing water, so I opened it and began pouring from it over my head. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people and praised Allah as He deserves, then said, ‘Now then.’ And she said: Some women of the Ansar made a noise, so I turned towards them to quiet them. I said to ‘A’ishah, ‘What did he say?’ She said: He said, ‘There is nothing that I had not been shown before that I have not seen at this place where I stand, even the Garden and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tried in the graves with a trial like, or close to, the trial of the false messiah. One of you will be approached and asked, “What do you know of this man?” As for the believer—or he said, the one who is certain; Hisham was unsure—he will say, “He is the Messenger of Allah. He is Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He brought us clear proofs and guidance, so we believed, responded, followed and affirmed the truth.” He will be told, “Sleep, righteous one. We already knew that you did indeed believe in him.” As for the hypocrite—or he said, the doubter; Hisham was unsure—he will be asked, “What do you know of this man?” He will say, “I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.”’

segments.arabic: قال هشام فلقد قالت لي فاطمة فأوعيته غير أنها ذكرت ما يغلظ عليه
segments.english: Hisham said: Fatimah did indeed tell it to me, and I retained it, except that she mentioned what would be made severe for him.

comparisons.note: The pinned 2.13.44 is the short Abu Sa‘id report, app 879; 2.13.45 is ‘Amr ibn Taghlib, app 881. Neither is this complete Asma’ report. Sunnah.com 922 is separately cited; its deprecated 44 label is not this EPUB body.

notes: Both prints read قالت قال at ‘A’ishah’s answer; the middle قال in the digital ما قال: قال: قال: is explicitly corrected to قالت. The two occurrences of Hisham’s uncertainty and the complete closing comment remain. The selected opening says Mahmud said, not Mahmud related to us; Brill’s Abu Bakr al-Siddiq expansion is not inserted. The selected affirmative فأوعيته follows the modern print, while Brill reads وما وعيته. This variant is retained and disclosed, not silently reconciled. The English comparisons attach the memory statement to Fatimah; the selected Arabic first-person closing remains Hisham’s speech, supported by al-‘Ayni’s discussion of the verb. No angels, names of questioners, or additional punishments are supplied. Modern printed reference: 922.

The pinned EPUB has no matching report between 2.13.44 (the short Abu Sa‘id account, app 879) and 2.13.45 (‘Amr ibn Taghlib, app 881). Sunnah.com 922 was separately read as an additional English comparison; its deprecated legacy 44 label does not identify the EPUB body. Bewley 880 is the directly matched primary English comparison. Independent review remains pending.

segments.arabic: [881] حدثنا محمد بن معمر قال: حدثنا أبو عاصم عن جرير بن حازم قال: سمعت الحسن يقول: حدثنا عمرو بن تغلب
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Ma‘mar related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim. He said: I heard al-Hasan saying: ‘Amr ibn Taghlib related to us:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ أتى بمال أو بسبي فقسمه فأعطى رجالا وترك رجالا فبلغه أن الذين ترك عتبوا فحمد الله ثم أثنى عليه، ثم قال: أما بعد فوالله إني لأعطي الرجل وأدع الرجل والذي أدع أحب إلي من الذي أعطى ولكن أعطي أقواما لما أرى في قلوبهم من الجزع والهلع وأكل أقواما إلى ما جعل الله في قلوبهم من الغنى والخير فيهم عمرو بن تغلب فوالله ما أحب أن لي بكلمة رسول الله ﷺ حمر النعم
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought wealth or captives. He divided it, giving to some men and leaving others. News reached him that those he had left were displeased. He praised Allah, then extolled Him, then said, ‘Now then. By Allah, I give to one man and leave another, although the one I leave is more beloved to me than the one I give to. But I give to some people because of the distress and anxiety I see in their hearts, and I entrust others to the contentment and goodness that Allah has placed in their hearts. Among them is ‘Amr ibn Taghlib.’ By Allah, I would not wish to have red camels in exchange for those words of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: تابعه يونس
segments.english: Yunus corroborated this.

notes: The wealth-or-captives alternative, distress and anxiety, inner contentment, oath, exchange for red camels and final Yunus corroboration all remain. Brill reads أو بشيء where the selected source and modern print have captives, and does not print the final Yunus line here; the selected and modern wording is retained. Khan paraphrases the gift as property or something and omits the Yunus line. Modern reference: 923.

segments.arabic: [882] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني عروة أن عائشة أخبرته
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ خرج ذات ليلة من جوف الليل فصلى في المسجد فصلى رجال بصلاته فأصبح الناس فتحدثوا فاجتمع أكثر منهم فصلوا معه فأصبح الناس فتحدثوا فكثر أهل المسجد من الليلة الثالثة فخرج رسول الله ﷺ فصلوا بصلاته فلما كانت الليلة الرابعة عجز المسجد عن أهله حتى خرج لصلاة الصبح فلما قضى الفجر أقبل على الناس فتشهد، ثم قال: أما بعد فإنه لم يخف علي مكانكم لكني خشيت أن تفرض عليكم فتعجزوا عنها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out one night in the middle of the night and prayed in the mosque. Some men prayed following his prayer. In the morning, the people spoke about it, and more of them gathered and prayed with him. In the morning, the people spoke about it, and the number of people in the mosque increased on the third night. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out, and they prayed following his prayer. On the fourth night, the mosque could not hold its people, until he came out for the dawn prayer. When he had finished the dawn prayer, he faced the people and pronounced the testimony of faith, then said, ‘Now then. Your presence was not hidden from me, but I feared that it would be made obligatory upon you and you would be unable to perform it.’

segments.arabic: تابعه يونس
segments.english: Yunus corroborated this.

notes: The full sequence of nights, repeated morning reports, two source honorifics and final corroboration remain. The short tashahhud verb is translated without inserting a full formula. No Tahajjud label, Ramadan setting or legal explanation from comparison glosses is added. Khan omits the Yunus line. Modern reference: 924.

segments.arabic: [883] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة عن أبي حميد الساعدي أنه أخبره
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: ‘Urwah informed me, from Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi, who informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قام عشية بعد الصلاة فتشهد وأثنى على الله بما هو أهله، ثم قال: أما بعد
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up one evening after the prayer, pronounced the testimony of faith and extolled Allah as He deserves, then said, ‘Now then.’

segments.arabic: تابعه أبو معاوية وأبو أسامة عن هشام عن أبيه عن أبي حميد عن النبي ﷺ قال: أما بعد
segments.english: Abu Mu‘awiyah and Abu Usamah corroborated this, from Hisham, from his father, from Abu Humayd, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said, ‘Now then.’

segments.arabic: تابعه العدني عن سفيان في أما بعد
segments.english: Al-‘Adani corroborated this, from Sufyan, concerning ‘Now then.’

notes: Both complete corroborating routes, all three occurrences of the transition formula and both source honorifics remain. Bewley shortens the first route and leaves al-‘Adani unnamed in the second; Khan omits both closing routes. Brill expands Abu Humayd to al-Sa‘idi in the closing route; the selected short name remains. Modern reference: 925.

segments.arabic: [884] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: حدثني علي بن حسين عن المسور بن مخرمة
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: ‘Ali ibn Husayn related to me, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah:

segments.arabic: قال قام رسول الله ﷺ فسمعته حين تشهد يقول أما بعد
segments.english: He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up, and I heard him saying, when he pronounced the testimony of faith, ‘Now then.’

segments.arabic: تابعه الزبيدي عن الزهري
segments.english: Al-Zubaydi corroborated this, from al-Zuhri.

notes: The individual related-to-me link and al-Zubaydi’s complete closing route remain. Bewley attributes corroboration to al-Zuhri without preserving al-Zubaydi; Khan omits it. Brill uses informed me in the opening route and al-Husayn rather than the selected Husayn; the selected form matches the modern print and is retained. Modern reference: 926.

segments.arabic: [885] حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبان قال: حدثنا ابن الغسيل قال: حدثنا عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: Isma‘il ibn Aban related to us. He said: Ibn al-Ghasil related to us. He said: ‘Ikrimah related to us, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

segments.arabic: قال صعد النبي ﷺ المنبر وكان آخر مجلس جلسه متعطفا ملحفة على منكبيه قد عصب رأسه بعصابة دسمة فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال أيها الناس إلي فثابوا إليه، ثم قال: أما بعد فإن هذا الحي من الأنصار يقلون ويكثر الناس فمن ولي شيئا من أمة محمد ﷺ فاستطاع أن يضر فيه أحدا أو ينفع فيه أحدا فليقبل من محسنهم ويتجاوز عن مسيئهم
segments.english: He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit. It was the last gathering in which he sat. He had wrapped a cloak around his shoulders and tied a dark headcloth around his head. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, ‘People, come to me.’ They gathered towards him. Then he said, ‘Now then. This community of the Ansar will become fewer, while the people become more numerous. Whoever takes charge of any part of the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and is able in that position to harm someone or benefit someone, should accept from those among them who do good and pardon those among them who do wrong.’

notes: The digital أمه is explicitly corrected to أمة, supported by both prints. The shorter selected Isma‘il ibn Aban is retained; Brill adds al-Warraq. Brill has one shoulder and omits the honorific after Muhammad, whereas the selected text and modern print have both shoulders and the honorific. The community, not its geographical area, becomes fewer. Dark headcloth follows the lexical colour reading of دسمة discussed by al-‘Ayni; the oily-cloth wording in both English comparisons and alternative lexical explanations are documented, not silently treated as unanimous. No cause, illness detail or legal qualification is inserted. Modern reference: 927.

segments.arabic: [886] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا بشر بن المفضل قال: حدثنا عبيد الله عن نافع عن عبد الله
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah:

segments.arabic: قال: كان النبي ﷺ يخطب خطبتين يقعد بينهما
segments.english: He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to deliver two sermons, sitting between them.

notes: The selected short names ‘Ubaydullah and ‘Abdullah remain; Brill expands them with ibn ‘Umar. The two sermons and intervening sitting are complete. Modern reference: 928.

segments.arabic: [887] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن الزهري عن أبي عبد الله الأغر عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu ‘Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: قال: قال النبي ﷺ إذا كان يوم الجمعة وقفت الملائكة على باب المسجد يكتبون الأول فالأول ومثل المهجر كمثل الذي يهدي بدنة ثم كالذي يهدي بقرة ثم كبشا ثم دجاجة ثم بيضة فإذا خرج الإمام طووا صحفهم ويستمعون الذكر
segments.english: He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘When Friday comes, the angels stand at the door of the mosque, recording the first to arrive, then the next. The likeness of the one who comes early is that of someone offering a camel, then someone offering a cow, then a ram, then a hen, then an egg. When the imam comes out, they fold up their sheets and listen to the remembrance.’

notes: All five successive offerings, arrival order, folded sheets and listening remain. No earliest-hour limit from Khan is added. Brill has an honorific for Abu Hurayrah that is absent from the selected and modern wording; it is not inserted. Modern reference: 929.

segments.arabic: [888] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن عمرو بن دينار عن جابر بن عبد الله
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah:

segments.arabic: قال جاء رجل والنبي ﷺ يخطب الناس يوم الجمعة، فقال أصليت يا فلان قال لا قال قم فاركع ركعتين
segments.english: He said: A man came while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was addressing the people on Friday. He said, ‘Have you prayed, so-and-so?’ He said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Stand up and pray two units of prayer.’

notes: The selected source explicitly ends with ركعتين, two units, while both printed occurrences end more briefly with قم فاركع. The selected fuller wording remains unchanged and is also present in the Khan comparison. Bewley ends with get up and pray. The unnamed address and negative answer are retained. Modern reference: 930.

segments.arabic: [889] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو سمع جابرا
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Amr, who heard Jabir:

segments.arabic: قال دخل رجل يوم الجمعة والنبي ﷺ يخطب، فقال أصليت قال لا قال قم فصل ركعتين
segments.english: He said: A man entered on Friday while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon. He said, ‘Have you prayed?’ He said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘Stand up and pray two units of prayer.’

notes: The answer is No in the selected Arabic and both prints, matching Khan. Bewley’s Yes is a comparison discrepancy and is not adopted. The selected final قم is preserved; the modern print omits it while Brill includes it. Brill expands ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah with al-Madini. Modern reference: 931.

segments.arabic: [890] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن عبد العزيز عن أنس وعن يونس عن ثابت عن أنس
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, from Anas; and from Yunus, from Thabit, from Anas:

segments.arabic: قال بينما النبي ﷺ يخطب يوم الجمعة إذ قام رجل، فقال: يا رسول الله هلك الكراع وهلك الشاء فادع الله أن يسقينا فمد يديه ودعا
segments.english: He said: While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on Friday, a man stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the horses have perished and the sheep have perished. Ask Allah to give us rain.’ He extended his hands and supplicated.

notes: Both Anas routes remain, including Yunus through Thabit. Brill expands ‘Abd al-‘Aziz with ibn Suhayb; the selected and modern short form remains. الكراع is rendered horses following the lexical discussion in al-Tawdih; sheep and both repeated perishing clauses remain. Hands are extended, not changed to arms or an added invocation formula. Modern reference: 932.

segments.arabic: [891] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا الوليد قال: حدثنا أبو عمرو قال: حدثني إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amr related to us. He said: Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah related to me, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: قال أصابت الناس سنة على عهد النبي ﷺ فبينا النبي ﷺ يخطب في يوم جمعة قام أعرابي، فقال: يا رسول الله هلك المال وجاع العيال فادع الله لنا فرفع يديه وما نرى في السماء قزعة فوالذي نفسي بيده ما وضعها حتى ثار السحاب أمثال الجبال ثم لم ينزل عن منبره حتى رأيت المطر يتحادر على لحيته ﷺ فمطرنا يومنا ذلك ومن الغد وبعد الغد والذي يليه حتى الجمعة الأخرى وقام ذلك الأعرابي أو قال غيره، فقال: يا رسول الله تهدم البناء وغرق المال فادع الله لنا فرفع يديه، فقال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا فما يشير بيده إلى ناحية من السحاب إلا انفرجت وصارت المدينة مثل الجوبة وسال الوادي قناة شهرا ولم يجئ أحد من ناحية إلا حدث بالجود
segments.english: He said: The people suffered a drought in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon one Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the dependants are hungry. Supplicate to Allah for us.’ He raised his hands, and we could see no patch of cloud in the sky. By Him in whose hand is my soul, he had not lowered them before clouds rose like mountains. Then he had not come down from his pulpit before I saw rain streaming down his beard, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rain fell upon us that day, the next day, the day after it and the day following, until the next Friday. That Bedouin—or he said, someone else—stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the buildings have collapsed and the livestock have drowned. Supplicate to Allah for us.’ He raised his hands and said, ‘Allah, around us and not upon us.’ Whenever he pointed his hand towards a part of the clouds, they parted. Madinah became like an opening, and the valley of Qanat flowed for a month. No one came from any direction without speaking of the abundant rain.

notes: Both prints read المال, not the digital الماء, in the first plea. This is a declared correction with the original preserved; al-Tawdih explains المال here as livestock. The cloud sequence remains before lowering the hands and the rain before descending the pulpit: the English comparisons do not consistently retain both temporal negatives. The possible different speaker, all four days, month-long valley flow and three honorifics remain. Brill expands al-Walid and Abu ‘Amr with ibn Muslim and al-Awza‘i, lacks the third honorific; those forms are not silently imported. Qanat is a named valley, not an invented water channel. Modern reference: 933.

segments.arabic: [892] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيب أن أبا هريرة أخبره
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurayrah informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إذا قلت لصاحبك يوم الجمعة أنصت والإمام يخطب فقد لغوت
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘If you say to your companion on Friday, “Listen quietly,” while the imam is delivering the sermon, you have engaged in idle speech.’

notes: Friday, the companion, the imam’s concurrent sermon and the precise idle-speech term remain; Khan’s broad evil-act paraphrase is not substituted. Brill adds an honorific for Abu Hurayrah absent from the selected and modern wording. Salman’s separate chapter context remains outside narration. Modern reference: 934.

segments.arabic: [893] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ ذكر يوم الجمعة، فقال: فيه ساعة لا يوافقها عبد مسلم وهو قائم يصلي يسأل الله تعالى شيئا إلا أعطاه إياه وأشار بيده يقللها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned Friday and said, ‘In it is a time that no Muslim servant meets while standing in prayer, asking Allah Most High for something, without Him giving it to him.’ He indicated with his hand how short it was.

notes: The standing posture, Muslim servant, request, response and singular hand indicating a short time remain. No clock-hour duration or precise time of day is supplied. The selected Most High is present in the modern print and absent from Brill; it remains. Modern reference: 935.

segments.arabic: [894] حدثنا معاوية بن عمرو قال: حدثنا زائدة عن حصين عن سالم بن أبي الجعد قال: حدثنا جابر بن عبد الله
segments.english: Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Husayn, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d. He said: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah related to us:

segments.arabic: قال بينما نحن نصلي مع النبي ﷺ إذ أقبلت عير تحمل طعاما فالتفتوا إليها حتى ما بقي مع النبي ﷺ إلا اثنا عشر رجلا فنزلت هذه الآية { وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما }
segments.english: He said: While we were praying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a caravan carrying food arrived. They turned towards it until only twelve men remained with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then this verse was revealed: ‘When they see trade or diversion, they disperse towards it and leave you standing.’

notes: The caravan is not assigned camels, an origin in Syria or a new explanation of the prayer from Khan’s additions. Both source honorifics, twelve men and only the quoted portion of Quran 62:11 remain. No verse continuation is inserted. Modern reference: 936.

segments.arabic: [895] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يصلي قبل الظهر ركعتين وبعدها ركعتين وبعد المغرب ركعتين في بيته وبعد العشاء ركعتين وكان لا يصلي بعد الجمعة حتى ينصرف فيصلي ركعتين
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray two units before the noon prayer and two units after it, two units after the sunset prayer in his house, and two units after the night prayer. He would not pray after Friday prayer until he had departed, then he would pray two units.

notes: All five pairs of prayer units remain. In his house stays attached to the sunset-prayer clause; no final at-home phrase from Khan is added after Friday prayer. Modern reference: 937.

segments.arabic: [896] حدثنا سعيد بن أبي مريم قال: حدثنا أبو غسان قال: حدثني أبو حازم عن سهل
segments.english: Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Abu Ghassan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to me, from Sahl:

segments.arabic: قال: كانت فينا امرأة تجعل على أربعاء في مزرعة لها سلقا فكانت إذا كان يوم جمعة تنزع أصول السلق فتجعله في قدر ثم تجعل عليه قبضة من شعير تطحنها فتكون أصول السلق عرقه وكنا ننصرف من صلاة الجمعة فنسلم عليها فتقرب ذلك الطعام إلينا فنلعقه وكنا نتمنى يوم الجمعة لطعامها ذلك
segments.english: He said: There was a woman among us who planted chard along irrigation channels in a field of hers. When Friday came, she would pull up the chard roots and put them in a pot. Then she would add a handful of barley that she ground, so the chard roots served as its meat. We would leave Friday prayer and greet her. She would bring that food near to us, and we would lick it up. We used to long for Friday because of that food of hers.

notes: The selected short Sahl is not expanded to Brill’s Sahl ibn Sa‘d. The selected grinding verb and عرقه, the meat metaphor, are retained; Brill has differing grinding and غَرِقَة readings. Ibn Hajar explicitly distinguishes the variants and explains irrigation channels and the meat-on-the-bone metaphor. The English preserves licking rather than inserting fingers, and does not add a new cooking action from comparison wording. Modern reference: 938.

segments.arabic: [897] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة قال: حدثنا ابن أبي حازم عن أبيه عن سهل
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from his father, from Sahl:

segments.arabic: بهذا، وقال: ما كنا نقيل ولا نتغدى إلا بعد الجمعة
segments.english: With this account, and he said: We would neither take our midday rest nor eat lunch until after Friday prayer.

notes: The source’s explicit backward pointer بهذا remains without copying 896’s body into this entry. The brief link above the text identifies the preceding account separately. Both the rest and lunch are retained. Brill expands Sahl to Sahl ibn Sa‘d; the selected and modern short form remains. Modern reference: 939.

segments.arabic: [898] حدثنا محمد بن عقبة الشيباني قال: حدثنا أبو إسحاق الفزاري عن حميد
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Uqbah al-Shaybani related to us. He said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, from Humayd:

segments.arabic: قال: سمعت أنسا يقول كنا نبكر إلى الجمعة ثم نقيل
segments.english: He said: I heard Anas saying: We used to go early to Friday prayer, then take our midday rest.

notes: The selected explicit I heard Anas saying matches the modern print; Brill instead has from Anas, who said. The selected early-going wording is not replaced by a before-zenith assertion or by the completed prayer wording in Khan. Modern reference: 940.

segments.arabic: [899] حدثنا سعيد بن أبي مريم قال: حدثنا أبو غسان قال: حدثني أبو حازم عن سهل
segments.english: Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Abu Ghassan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to me, from Sahl:

segments.arabic: قال كنا نصلي مع النبي ﷺ الجمعة ثم تكون القائلة
segments.english: He said: We used to pray the Friday prayer with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and afterwards would come the midday rest.

notes: The section’s final complete report retains the Prophet honorific and the order of prayer then rest. Brill expands Sahl to Sahl ibn Sa‘d; the selected modern short form remains. This closes the selected Friday Prayer inventory, not the entire Bukhari collection. Modern reference: 941.
